entries.summary: Grip documents a diff-explanation quiz, an optional Git pre-push hook and coding-agent integrations. A model grades the developer's explanation of a change; the score does not certify code correctness or security.
entries.selection_context: Compare workflows for discussing and explaining a diff before pushing it. Check which provider receives code changes and answers, and how the hook is enabled or bypassed.
entries.limitations: The fake provider uses answer length or the word "because" to demonstrate the flow; it does not assess understanding. Review provider data handling, hook bypass behavior and team thresholds. No code-quality, security or runtime validation was performed.
entries.decision: Retain the published route as a dated unranked reference when absent from the current discovery snapshot.

entries.summary: Lucarne documents a local-agent mobile notification and control bridge through Telegram and WeChat. Its README explicitly describes setup without hooks, skills or MCP. Feishu appears only on the README roadmap.
entries.selection_context: Compare mobile notifications, session continuation and approval routing for local coding agents. Treat this as an agent-control bridge when assessing its fit.
entries.limitations: Review authorized users, chat access, session-history exposure, bot credentials and approval routing before enabling remote control. The broader repository description mentions Feishu, but the reviewed README lists it as planned. Privacy, authorization enforcement and runtime behavior were not independently tested.
entries.decision: Retain the published route as a dated unranked reference when absent from the current discovery snapshot.
